account:
Today has seemed mostly routine, although I still have a feeling I may be missing something. The only unusual reports concern the bakery: the neighbour heard people mention bakery lights, and Townsfolk Ten reported the baker carrying a sack of bread at the bridge around midmorning. The secretary also saw the baker near the bridge carrying bread around ten thirty-six, but did not establish a destination or companion. The neighbour says the baker described fresh bread coming to market and knew of no special occasion. Nobody has reported bread shortages or unusual evening activity to the secretary. These observations could simply reflect normal baking and deliveries; I have no evidence of a secret gathering or wrongdoing. The neighbour promised to report anything personally observed along the docks at our three o'clock tea.

At the accounts appointment, the builder reported visual checks of the bridge, landing, and warehouse approach found no confirmed defects, and no money was spent. Freight has offered warehouse and ferry services, but no transport is authorized or needed yet. I have authorized no repair spending. The secretary is recording that decision but says they have not seen an accounts ledger and cannot verify the treasury balance or commitments. I need to establish those facts rather than assume them. The innkeeper has now arrived at the office; I have asked their business and await an answer. I do not yet know whether their visit concerns ordinary trade or anything else.
